doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Technology, blank media and surviving as a small label
summary: Purdie says big companies profit from blanks and control, while he survives on small sales of his own label.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Technology has hurt them and it’s helped them. The only way for them to survive what they’re doing, they’re making it on technology. They are actually selling more blank tapes and CDs than they are songs and records and CDs. They’re actually selling more blanks. They are making their money selling blanks.

And they all talk about the download, that they’re not getting paid. They’re getting paid. They’re not getting paid enough as far as they’re concerned. So they are still making the money on the blanks. And it’s only the big guys who make the blanks. The little guy can’t. He can’t because he can’t survive because he’s still got to buy from the big guy because they own the plants. So if you’re going to buy what they call off the rack it’s going to cost you. When you buy a blank today, you buy ten blanks. You buy fifty blanks. You buy a hundred blanks. But how much does it cost you? Is it a dollar a blank? Is it two dollars a blank? Is it fifty cents a blank? It all depends on how many you’re going to make and how many you’re going to sell. How long is it going to take to sell them? So the big guys are still making the money. It’s all about control. That’s what it is.

They made the units to whereas we want something, people are not going to make more than a hundred blanks a year for selling purposes. They’re not making them for selling purposes, they’re making them to give away. Because it becomes expensive. Just buy blanks and make a blank for your friend. But it’s a hobby. It’s not a business. So a little guy with a little record label, if I sell five or ten thousand units I’m doing quite well. Well I’ve been doing that for some time and staying away from the big guys and how I’ve survived and still be able to chill out. And still be able to play music and not have all the problems that most people have of staying healthy or being able to travel around the world and enjoy yourself and have a good time doing it. I’m doing that. And I am enjoying it. I like meeting the people. I like being on both sides of the fence. So it’s okay because I’m just being me. Well the big guys are now looking at me. And it’s a little scary. But I’m ready for them now. I’m ready to say okay, all right Dad, take care of me. I’m ready now. I’m ready to accept the inevitable. It’s okay. You know I had a little fun, it was good, I enjoyed myself, I’m ready to get in line and follow and do what you tell me to do.
